Union money resolves to the line item; state money resolves to the Police major head per state (and prisons per state from NCRB), with strength and per-capita figures reported: while BPR&D is down; city money does not exist outside Delhi Police, and city strength has no primary while BPR&D is down — cities get the footprint (installations, commissionerate entities with reported: strength) and the void. entities.label: Seventh Central Pay Commission (pay matrix, 2016)
entities.sub: Report Nov 2015; Cabinet approval 29 Jun 2016; effective 1 Jan 2016; separate Defence Pay Matrix; Military Service Pay
entities.publicRole: The rule that fixes every uniformed salary in this fleet: the Defence Pay Matrix for the three services and the civil matrix adopted by the CAPFs and, with state modifications, by state police.
d: Report of the Seventh CPC (Nov 2015): Pay Bands and Grade Pay replaced by a pay matrix; separate matrices for civilians, Defence Forces personnel and Military Nursing Service; fitment factor 2.57 (new minimum ₹18,000 ÷ old minimum ₹7,000) [documented]

Defence Pay Matrix commences at Level 3 (old GP 2000, the induction level for Sepoys and equivalent) with entry pay ₹21,700; levels unique to the defence forces: 5A, 10B, 12A, 13A (old GP 3400, 6100, 8000, 8900) [documented]

Military Service Pay recommended at ₹15,500 (Service Officers up to Brigadier), ₹10,800 (Nursing Officers), ₹5,200 (JCO/ORs), ₹3,600 (Non-Combatants Enrolled, IAF) per month, up from ₹6,000/₹4,200/₹2,000/₹1,000; counted for DA and pension, not for HRA or increment [documented]

Cabinet of 29 Jun 2016 approved pay and pension recommendations effective 1 Jan 2016; stated beneficiaries over 1 crore: 47 lakh employees (14 lakh defence) and 53 lakh pensioners (18 lakh defence); arrears paid within FY2016-17 [documented]
The Commission's own costing: additional ₹1,02,100 crore in 2016-17 over business-as-usual (pay ₹39,100 cr, allowances ₹29,300 cr, pension ₹33,700 cr), 23.55% above BAU [documented]

entities.label: Agnipath scheme (2022)
entities.sub: Four-year enrolment of Agniveers below officer rank in the three services; Cabinet approval 14 Jun 2022; no pension or gratuity; Seva Nidhi ₹11.71 lakh; up to 25% retained
entities.publicRole: The largest change to the terms of the soldier's contract since Independence; its budget line is printed per service in Demand 20.
d: Cabinet approved on 14 Jun 2022: enrolment for four years under the Service Acts as a distinct rank; package ₹30,000 (yr 1), ₹33,000, ₹36,500, ₹40,000 (yr 4) a month, 70% in hand, 30% to the Agniveer Corpus Fund matched by the Government; Seva Nidhi about ₹11.71 lakh tax-free on exit; life cover ₹48 lakh; 'no entitlement to gratuity and pensionary benefits'; up to 25% of each batch enrolled in the regular cadre for a further minimum 15 years; age 17.5-21; 46,000 to be recruited in 2022 [documented]

The Ministry's stated case (same release): a 'youthful profile' with average age falling 4-5 years, 'tech savvy' forces, skilled youth 'ploughed back' into society; the release states no saving figure [documented]
Demand 20 'Agnipath Scheme' sub-heads: Army actual 2024-25 ₹6,216.74 cr, BE 2026-27 ₹15,173.68 cr; Navy ₹544.65 cr → ₹1,150.50 cr; Air Force ₹698.36 cr → ₹1,072.00 cr [documented]

Headcounts: Army oral evidence to the Standing Committee (Mar 2025) 'currently, 1,23,000 Agniveers are enrolled'; Navy 11,634 Agniveers (1,718 women); IAF airmen strength 1,39,876 including Agniveervayu on 1 Oct 2024 plus 1,982 Agniveervayu trainees; Navy 1,321 women Agniveers borne (Dec 2024) [documented]

Objections on record: Congress manifesto 2024 'will scrap the Agnipath Scheme and return to the normal recruitment processes'; Kharge letter to the President 26 Feb 2024 ('parallel cadres', 'discrimination in death'); veterans quoted by The Tribune (Jul 2024): four years too short to make an effective soldier, 25% retention a 'double-edged weapon' [documented/reported]

entities.label: One Rank One Pension (OROP)
entities.sub: MoD letter 12(1)/2014/D(Pen/Pol)-Part-II of 7 Nov 2015, effective 1 Jul 2014; re-fixed every five years (2019 base revision approved 23 Dec 2022); upheld by the Supreme Court 16 Mar 2022
entities.publicRole: The equalisation rule inside the Defence Pensions demand; its recurring cost is printed by the Ministry.
d: Order of 7 Nov 2015: pension of past pensioners re-fixed on the average of minimum and maximum pension of 2013 retirees of the same rank and length of service, effective 1 Jul 2014; those above the average protected; arrears in four half-yearly instalments (one for family pensioners and gallantry awardees); re-fixation every five years [documented]

Cost as stated by the Ministry: arrears ₹10,795.40 crore to 20,60,220 pensioners/family pensioners (2015-16 ₹2,861.55 cr; 2016-17 ₹5,370.61 cr; 2017-18 ₹2,563.24 cr); recurring about ₹7,123.38 crore a year; 'approx. ₹57,000 crore' in eight years to Dec 2022 [documented]

Revision approved by Cabinet 23 Dec 2022 w.e.f. 1 Jul 2019 on 2018 retirees: 25.13 lakh beneficiaries (4.52 lakh new); additional ₹8,450 crore a year at 31% DR; arrears Jul 2019-Jun 2022 about ₹23,638 crore; sepoy pension ₹17,699 → ₹19,726, havildar ₹20,066 → ₹21,782, Lt Col ₹84,330 → ₹95,400, Lt Gen ₹1,01,515 → ₹1,12,050 a month [documented]

Supreme Court (WP(C) 419/2016, 16 Mar 2022, Chandrachud, Surya Kant, Vikram Nath JJ): the 7 Nov 2015 definition is not arbitrary; no constitutional mandate of OROP is read into Nakara or SPS Vains; re-fixation from 1 Jul 2019 directed within three months [documented]

Pre-2015 record (PIB e-booklet): the 4th, 5th and 6th CPCs, the 2004 Inter-Ministerial Committee, the 2005 GoM and the Cabinet Secretary committees of 2009 and 2012 did not recommend OROP; the K.P. Singh Dev Committee (1984), the Standing Committee on Defence and the Rajya Sabha Petitions Committee (142nd Report) favoured it; ₹1,000 crore provided in Budget 2014-15 [documented]

claims.d: Judicial ruling on pay-pensions:c014: Indian Ex Servicemen Movement v. Union of India, D.Y. Chandrachud, Surya Kant and Vikram Nath JJ. Agniveers were already about 11% of Army JCO/OR strength by Mar 2025.
narratives.strongestCounter: The Army told the Standing Committee (Mar 2025) the scheme is 'the most transformative reform' and is 'progressing on the path to make it successful'; the Ministry's stated aim is a younger, tech-savvy profile; the first exits only begin in 2026-27, so no outcome data exists either way; retention policy can be changed by notification.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: The first batch's actual retention rate (2026-27), any Service survey released, or a Standing Committee finding on training and cohesion.

symmetryCheck: Same lens, both governments, from the demands themselves: service pay ÷ Capital Outlay actual was 0.88 in 2009-10 and 0.78 in 2013-14 (UPA-II, Antony) and 0.90 in 2024-25 (NDA, Rajnath Singh; 0.94 with the Agnipath line), with BE 2026-27 at 0.68 (0.76 with Agnipath): the ratio is flat and the only numerator shocks are the 6th CPC arrears (2009-10) and the Agnipath line (2024-25 →). What moved is pensions — 3.47× from actual 2013-14 to 2024-25 against 2.33× for service pay and 2.02× for capital — driven by the 7th CPC (2016), OROP (2014/2019) and dearness relief, decisions taken under both governments (OROP accepted in the 2014 President's address and provided ₹1,000 cr in Budget 2014-15 by the incoming government; the 7th CPC was constituted under UPA-II in 2014 and implemented under NDA in 2016). On the contract with soldiers, the Congress objects to Agnipath and promises OROP 'in letter and spirit'; the BJP government defends Agnipath and has paid OROP on the 2015 definition the Supreme Court upheld; identical fields were used for the objection, the Army's answer and the petitioners' contention beside the Court's holding. On states, only Uttar Pradesh (BJP-run) yielded a primary salary share (53.7% of MH 2055 actual 2024-25) and only Bihar (NDA-run) a primary constable pay level (Level 3 ₹21,700); opposition-run West Bengal and Tamil Nadu portals never opened, so no cross-party comparison of pay is made and the asymmetry is recorded as a void rather than a finding. On CAPF outcomes the lens produced rates (14.1 suicides per lakh in 2024; 1.18% VR/resignation) that are workload indicators with two official readings (the Ministry's domestic/health/financial factors; the Committee's working conditions), neither adopted.
